summary: CosmicValley is a client-side decision-support web platform for the Field Shift challenge that turns NASA Earth-observation telemetry into actionable 3-year crop rotation and off-season cover-crop plans. Selecting any parcel on a 3D globe or 2D map fuses 10-year NASA POWER agroclimatology, MODIS Terra NDVI bare-soil detection, SMAP, CERES, GPM IMERG, and SRTM/Copernicus terrain with ISRIC SoilGrids v2.0, Sentinel-2 / USGS NLCD arable masks, and USDA SSURGO. An in-browser ONNX Random Forest model (21 crops, 5-fold spatial block CV) works with a deterministic FAO-56 Penman-Monteith water-balance and N/SOC carryover engine to compare three switchable priorities (Soil Regeneration, Water Conservation, Maximum Yield) directly against a 3-year monocrop baseline across Dry/Baseline/Wet scenarios, disclose Out-of-Distribution (OOD) uncertainty, and export a personalized PDF plan. Core code was built by the team with SI coding/proofreading assistance and 26 SI-watermarked WebP crop visuals.
details:
Source Code Repository: https://github.com/arkadiychulkover/CosmicFarmers

CosmicValley bridges the gap between raw satellite Earth observations and practical parcel-level crop planning for farmers and extension agronomists in Ukraine and globally. Running 100% in the browser with zero backend servers or paid API keys required, the platform guides users through three stages:

1. Field Configuration & Arable Land Verification (/):

Users pick any farm coordinate on a 3D WebGL globe (Three.js) or an interactive 2D map picker (OpenStreetMap + NASA GIBS canvas slippy map with Nominatim search, or optional Google Maps JS API), or start from curated presets (Poltava Steppe in Ukraine, Iowa Corn Belt in USA, Andalusia in Spain, or Random Arable Field). Global Sentinel-2 10m land cover, U.S. USGS NLCD 30m / USDA CropScape CDL (CONUS), and OpenStreetMap Overpass checks automatically verify whether coordinates fall on cultivated cropland and warn on water, forest, wetland, or urban surfaces. Topsoil pH, SOC, Total N, and texture are fetched in physical units from ISRIC SoilGrids v2.0 (with USDA SSURGO fallback in CONUS) and can be manually overridden from local lab tests.

2. Live NASA Telemetry & Climate Stress Simulator (/telemetry):

CosmicValley loads growing-season-aligned metrics (Mar–Oct Northern Hemisphere / cross-year May–Apr Southern Hemisphere) separating 8-month seasonal vs. 12-month annual precipitation, 10-year rainfall percentiles (p25, p50, p75), root-zone moisture (GWETROOT), extreme storm days (>= 25 mm/day), canopy heat-stress days (>= 32 °C), SMAP/TS-proxy freeze-thaw transitions, CERES solar flux, and decoded in-browser MODIS Terra NDVI profiles (NDVI < 0.25 flagging bare-soil months). A unified 12-month Risk Calendar and interactive Δ Temperature (°C) / Δ Rainfall (%) sliders let users stress-test resilience.

3. 3-Year Rotation Engine, 4-Strategy Comparison & PDF Export (/results):

An in-browser WebAssembly onnxruntime-web Random Forest classifier (trained on 2,402 global observations across 21 crops using 21 raw agro-edaphic features and validated via 5°×5° StratifiedGroupKFold spatial block CV) runs sequentially with an agronomic scoring, multi-year N/SOC carryover, and FAO-56 Penman-Monteith (ET0, Kc, SCS Peff, Saxton & Rawls AWC) engine. Instead of black-box recommendations, CosmicValley compares 4 strategies side-by-side — Existing Monocrop Baseline, Soil Regeneration, Water Conservation, and Maximum Yield — showing quantified trade-offs (ΔSOC g/kg, ΔN, m³/ha water demand), rationale, off-season cover crops (Winter Rye, Crimson Clover, Hairy Vetch, Oilseed Radish, Oats + Field Pea), explicit data-gap/fallback/OOD warnings for local agronomic review, Dry/Baseline/Wet precipitation scenarios, and one-click vector PDF export (Crop Plan PDF).

Representative Benchmark — Poltava Oblast, Ukraine (49.645° N, 34.421° E, Rainfed, Prev: Maize, Goal: Soil Regeneration):

- Verified Sentinel-2 rangeland/arable check, SRTM/Copernicus DEM 104 m elevation / 4.12% slope, Chernozem SOC 22.7 g/kg, AWC 168 mm/m, 351 mm 8-mo vs. 469 mm 12-mo rain, MODIS NDVI flagging Jan–Feb bare-soil risk (< 0.25).

- Recommended 3-year trajectory (Confidence 92/100): Soybean → Wheat (bridged by Oilseed Radish cover crop) → Soybean (bridged by Winter Rye), yielding Soil Health 95/100 (+0.4 g/kg ΔSOC, 0 unbridged bare months) and Dry/Baseline/Wet stress metrics.

Tools, Visuals & Use of Super Intelligence (SI):

Built with Svelte 5, Vite 6, JavaScript/TypeScript, Three.js, onnxruntime-web, jsPDF, Python (scikit-learn / skl2onnx), and verified by 47 automated Vitest unit, agronomy, geospatial, and UI tests. Core architecture, satellite data pipelines, ML training, and agronomy logic were authored by our team; Super Intelligence (SI) tools assisted only with edge-case debugging, formula cross-checking, and English proofreading. All 26 crop card visuals (1204×672 WebP) carry visible SI watermarks without NASA branding: 13 generated via Google Gemini ("Gemini · SI") and 13 generated via Grok ("Grok · SI" + native corner mark), all disclosed in the in-app Data Sources dialog and PDF report.
